tasks.short: Check which fluids the operation needs, collect and warm fluids, collect blood products and check them with the anaesthetist, keep fluids supplied during the operation, and record fluids used.

steps.what: Surgical technologist checks the fluids needed on the paper preference card
Surgical technologist collects saline and glucose from the store and warms them
Surgical technologist collects plasma or blood from the blood bank and checks it with the anaesthetist
Surgical technologist maintains the supply of fluids during the operation
Surgical technologist records the fluids used: on the paper list today, by scanning each fluid and blood product into the operation record after the change

tasks.design: The surgeon's preference card is kept in the OR module of the patient record ({OTHER}) per procedure, so the fluids needed show with the day's list. Fluids and blood products used are scanned by barcode into the operation record instead of being written down. Collecting, warming, the two-person blood check and keeping fluids supplied stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preference cards were paper and fluids used were written on a list.
tasks.enabler_now: OR modules hold preference cards and scan barcodes into the operation record.
tasks.still_hard: Bleeding changes fluid needs in minutes, which no card predicts.
tasks.human_edge: Having blood ready before the surgeon asks for it.

reach.learn: Whether the scanned record is complete.

evidence.claim: OR modules in patient records can hold preference cards and record scanned products in the operation record.
The medical dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the operation plan to the fluid record; ordering fluids for the store is outside.
Input contract: preference cards kept by surgeons and OR staff; barcodes on fluids and blood products; fallback is paper.

Collecting, checking and supplying keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because the card shows with the day's list instead of being looked up on paper, and reading it stays. s5 keeps 30 for scanning each item, which replaces writing names and numbers; the scan is the technologist's own record.
The blood bank's own checks do not change.
research_questions: Is the fluid record complete more often?

incremental.description: Surgical technologist updates preference cards after changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: preference cards in the OR module are often out of date, so the technologist still checks with the team and s1 keeps 80 (6.0); high: cards are kept current (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect surgery requests, check pre-operative screening and consent, build the OR schedule, agree it with surgeons and anaesthetists, finalise the day list, and inform patients of date and fasting.

steps.what: Surgical technologist collects surgery requests from surgeons on paper and by e-mail
Surgeon places the surgery request as an order in the patient record
Surgical technologist checks each patient's pre-operative screening and consent
Surgical technologist schedules surgical procedures on the OR planning board
Surgical technologist agrees the schedule with surgeons and anaesthetists
Surgical technologist finalises the day list
Surgical technologist checks each patient's message against the final day list: date, arrival time, fasting instructions and the patient's portal account
Surgical technologist releases the checked date and fasting messages to the patients' portal
Surgical technologist phones patients who do not use the portal with the date and fasting instructions

tasks.design: Surgeons place surgery requests as orders in the patient record ({OTHER}), and a worklist shows each patient's screening and consent status. The planning board estimates each procedure's duration from the surgeon's past cases and flags overbooked sessions. After the schedule is agreed and the technologist has finalised the day list, the technologist checks each patient's message against it and releases the messages once through the patient portal; patients who do not use the portal still get a call. Agreeing the schedule stays with the technologist and the team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came on paper and by e-mail, durations were guessed and patients were phoned one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: OR planning modules estimate durations from past cases and send portal messages.
tasks.still_hard: Emergencies break the schedule every day.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which surgeon always runs over and planning for it.
tasks.altitude: The technologist adjusts a checked schedule instead of building it by hand.

reach.learn: Whether fewer patients arrive not fasted.

evidence.claim: OR planning modules can estimate procedure durations from past cases and send patient portal messages.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from surgery requests to patients informed; the operation itself is outside.
Input contract: requests ordered by surgeons; screening status from the pre-operative clinic; fallback is paper and phone.
Patients read the portal message in about the time a call took; no added patient time.

Agreeing and finalising the schedule, the message check and the release keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 because orders replace collecting paper and e-mail, with emergencies still phoned in; s2 keeps 60 because the worklist shows status and checking stays; s3 keeps 70 because durations are estimated and overbooking is flagged, while the technologist still plans. s6p keeps 15 for the share of patients who do not use the portal. The surgeon's order (s1o) is other-role time.
research_questions: Do cancellations on the day fall?

incremental.description: No separate upkeep: calls to patients without the portal are kept in s6p.

approvals.approved_version: Each patient's message with operation date, arrival time and fasting instructions exactly as checked by the technologist in s5b against the final day list, sent once to that patient's portal account; any change to the day list needs a new check and message.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients do not use the portal and surgeons still e-mail many requests, so s6p keeps 50 and s1 keeps 60 (26.8); high: most patients use the portal and requests come as orders (35.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check stock of sterile supplies, write the order list, check it against coming operations, place the order, and arrange loan sets and implants with suppliers.

steps.what: Surgical technologist checks stock of sterile supplies in the OR store: by counting shelves today, by scanning the cards of empty bins after the change
Surgical technologist writes the order list for surgical supplies
Surgical technologist checks the order against the coming operations
Surgical technologist checks the final order: items, quantities against coming operations, supplier and delivery date
Surgical technologist releases the checked order to suppliers in the purchasing system: by typing it today, by one release after the change
Surgical technologist checks the loan set and implant request: operation, sets, sizes and the supplier to call
Surgical technologist arranges loan sets and implants with suppliers by phone

tasks.design: The OR store runs a two-bin system: scanning the barcode of an empty bin adds it to an order proposal in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), so shelves are not counted. The technologist checks the proposal against coming operations, checks the final order and releases it once to suppliers electronically. Arranging loan sets and implants for special cases stays a call with the supplier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shelves were counted and orders typed from handwritten lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Two-bin scanning and purchasing systems create order proposals and send them electronically.
tasks.still_hard: Loan sets for rare procedures need personal contact with suppliers.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that next week's list needs an implant size not in stock.
tasks.altitude: The technologist checks proposed orders instead of counting shelves.

evidence.claim: Two-bin systems with barcode scans can create order proposals in purchasing systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from the OR store to the order placed; receiving deliveries and paying invoices are outside.
Input contract: bin sizes set by the OR and purchasing; supplier catalogues in the purchasing system; fallback is counting and typing.

Checking against the schedule, both final checks and arranging loan sets keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for the round scanning empty bins; s2 keeps 30 for adding items outside the bins; s4 keeps 10 for the release.
research_questions: Do operations wait for missing supplies less often?

incremental.description: Surgical technologist adjusts bin sizes after shortages.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items, quantities, supplier and delivery date exactly as checked by the technologist in s3b, sent once electronically to that supplier; any change needs a new check.
The loan sets and implants with sizes and operation date exactly as checked by the technologist in s4b, requested once from the named supplier; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special items stay outside the bins, so they are still counted and typed and s1 keeps 70, s2 keeps 60 (27.7); high: standard supplies run on bins as designed (43.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record instrument and sponge counts, record implants and lot numbers, record times and devices in the operation record, check it is complete, file it, and file set and sterilisation labels.

steps.what: Surgical technologist records instrument and sponge counts on the paper count sheet
Surgical technologist records implants and lot numbers: by sticking labels and writing in the paper file today, by scanning each implant barcode after the change
Surgical technologist maintains records of surgical procedures: times, positioning and devices used
Surgical technologist checks the operation record is complete
Surgical technologist files the operation record in the patient file: on paper today, by saving it in the record after the change
Surgical technologist files instrument set and sterilisation labels: by sticking them in the file today, by scanning each set after the change

tasks.design: The OR module of the patient record ({OTHER}) takes counts on screen during the two-person count (this takes the same time as the paper sheet), implant identifiers and lot numbers by barcode scan, and times from the OR's own time stamps, with a template per procedure for positioning and devices. Instrument sets are scanned so the sterilisation batch links to the patient. Once the technologist has checked the record complete, they save it in the patient file; this is their own save in the same system and needs no approval. The counts themselves stay a two-person check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts, implant stickers and set labels lived on paper sheets filed with the record.
tasks.enabler_now: OR modules record counts, scan implants and sets, and take time stamps.
tasks.still_hard: Busy emergencies leave entries for after the operation.
tasks.human_edge: Insisting on a recount when something feels off.
tasks.altitude: The technologist checks the record instead of writing it.

reach.learn: Whether set tracing to patients is complete.

evidence.claim: OR modules can record counts on screen, scan implant identifiers and instrument sets, and take time stamps.
The medical dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.

assumptions: Boundary: from counts done and implants used to the record filed; billing is outside.
Input contract: barcodes on implants and sets; time stamps from the OR system; fallback is paper sheets and stickers.

The two-person count, recording the counts and checking the record keep their full time. s2 keeps 20 for scanning implants; s3 keeps 70 because time stamps come from the OR and the template gives standard positioning, and the technologist still records what was done; s5 keeps 20 for the save; s6 keeps 40 for scanning sets.
Scanners are within reach in every OR.
research_questions: Are operation records complete at first check?

incremental.description: Surgical technologist enters items whose barcode does not scan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older ORs have no scanner within reach, so half of implants and sets are still labelled by hand and s2 keeps 60, s6 keeps 70 (24.0); high: scanners in every OR (38.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The surgical technologist keeps supplying fluids, checking blood, agreeing schedules, arranging loan sets and counting; paper cards, phone calls, shelf counts and paper records shrink.
skills_to_grow: Scanning and checking the operation record
role.ambitious_version: A technologist with more attention on the patient and the operating field.
